title: A declarative update action answers 404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND where the data update on the same row answers 403 PERMISSION_DENIED
body:
domain:devx#3 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cz3RTQjLh7hZBLzgtZ

Filing gate: ③ an out-of-scope finding (class b) from the #30802 dev's measurement (os-dev-report 6678640069, PR #30846). ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested grade: p2. Routing is triage's.

## What happens

A caller who can read an object but has no edit grant on it, writing one row they cannot see (server 18.3.0, `main` `c17719dd`, measured on a booted app):

| Door | Answer |
|---|---|
| MCP `update_record`, REST `PATCH /api/v1/data/...` | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| MCP `run_action` on a declarative `update` action (`decide_approval_step`) | 404 `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` |
| MCP `get_record` | 404 `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` |

The same holds for an id that does not exist (`as_nope`): the data door says 403, the action door 404. With an edit grant, both doors answer 404 on the unreadable row. On a row the caller can see but not edit, both answer 403.

Evidence: `/mnt/project-files/pm-devx-seat3-30802/measurement/measure.out` (project files; the probe script sits beside it).

## Why it matters

- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`: a declarative update fires with the caller's permissions "exactly as for a user edit". The two doors disagree, so that sentence is false today.
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`: "Refusals come before the record lookup". The action door looks the record up first.
- A scenario card cannot state one expected refusal for this operation (#30802's `travel_expense` / `employee_approves_colleague` question is with the maintainer now).

## Seam

`spec:` action `operation: 'update'` → `runtime:` `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` `invokeBusinessAction` (`loadActionSubjectRecord` + `refuseDeniedSubjectLoad` before the write).

Dedupe words: declarative update action, run_action, refuseDeniedSubjectLoad, RECORD_NOT_FOUND vs PERMISSION_DENIED, action door permission order. Not searched beyond the dev's words: triage to confirm.
